name: Typeform
description: Typeform responses become Form Submitted events on the respondent's profile, with the answers you choose to copy. Only the email, a consent question you map and those answers are kept; everything else in a response is dropped before it's stored. A response never subscribes anyone.

signature_secret.label: Typeform webhook secret
signature_secret.help: A random value you choose, for example the output of: openssl rand -hex 20. Set the same value as the webhook's secret in Typeform.

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL.
Pick a random secret and save it as the integration's signing secret.
In Typeform, open the form → Connect → Webhooks → Add a webhook. Paste the webhook URL, open Edit, turn on Secret and paste the same secret, and turn the webhook on.

If the form has more than one email question, set email_field in the integration's settings to the ref of the one to use. If it has a yes/no or legal question asking for marketing consent, set consent_field to that question's ref; the answer is recorded on each Form Submitted event as marketing_consent. Set copy_fields to the refs of the answers worth keeping on the event, for example ["readable_ref_choice"]. Nothing else from a response is stored: hidden fields, other answers and typed "Other" choices are dropped.
Send a test response (Typeform's View deliveries → Send test request) and check the delivery log.

People this adds are held back from marketing. A form submission isn't an opt-in, so nobody is subscribed. To add people who ticked the consent question to your marketing, send them a confirmation (double opt-in) first.
